newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Feb 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Feb 24.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Bangladesh press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina on Sunday urged the opposition political parties to maintain peace and stability in the country to help attract foreign investment.
The government is learnt to have conveyed to the Thailand authorities about the holding of an international peace conference on Chittagong Hill Tracts, sponsored by some NGOs, in Bangkok.

Privatisation, banking sector reforms and water resources development are likely to feature the two-day donors' meeting beginning in Dhaka on Tuesday for a review of the new government's development performances.
Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina said foreign investment worth Taka 30 billion was in the pipeline.

The standing committee of the opposition Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) in an emergency meeting on Sunday decided to launch a vigorous anti-government movement in view of what it said repression and autocratic activities of the ruling party.
Three Bangladeshi nationals were killed in a road accident in the Indian city of Joypur last week.
Banque Indosuez has doubled its capital 400 million taka in Bangladesh for expansion of its operation, the bank's chairman for the South Asia and Pacific Jean-Claud Gruffat said in Dhaka on Sunday.
Hong Kong Bank, a member of UK-based HSBC which is the world's largest financial services institution, started its operation in Bangladesh on Sunday.
